builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/ap: The Anthropic API key. When omitted, read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/ba: A custom API base URL, for a proxy or internal endpoint. When omitted, read `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from the environment. When neither exists, use the Anthropic official endpoint, the claude CLI default behavior.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/en: Extra environment variables for the Claude Code process. Values remain only at runtime and do not enter result carry identity. A non-sensitive value that changes behavior must also appear in Experiment Flags or the owning Plugin's identity.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/ma: The maximum number of tool-use turns, passed to `--max-turns`. It limits Eval cost; when omitted, the CLI native default is unlimited.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/mc: Extra MCP servers, written to user-level `~/.claude.json` during each Sandbox before. The stdio form writes `command`, optionally with `args` / `env`. The Streamable HTTP form writes `url`, optionally with `headers`, copied verbatim into request headers, as a `{ "type": "http", "url": …, "headers": … }` entry.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/sk: Skills installed in the Sandbox: a local directory or file, or a Repo with a pinnable ref and optional enabled subset. They go to project-level `.claude/skills/<name>/`, where the claude CLI discovers them natively.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/pl: Native Claude Code Plugins: first connect a Marketplace, then install the named Plugin from it.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/se: The path to a complete official-format Claude Code `settings.json` in the local project. It resolves relative to the project root that runs niceeval—the directory containing `niceeval.config.ts`—not inside the Sandbox. It accepts only a relative path within the project root. A path containing `..`, an absolute path, a `~` path, or a symlink that resolves outside the project root errors during before. Its original bytes are uploaded verbatim as the otherwise-empty user-level `~/.claude/settings.json` in the Sandbox. It does not inherit host configuration, concatenate, or reserialize. Reserved keys `model` and `env` cause a before error when present. The manifest records only the project-relative path and byte SHA-256, not the contents.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/be: User Hooks run in array order after installation. They reuse SandboxCommand's narrow context and run only after settings are written, MCP attached, Skills and Plugins installed, and the manifest written. They suit process actions that can run only after installed artifacts are ready, such as a Plugin's before script. A throw counts as an infrastructure error (`attempt errored`). See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
builtin-agent-config/ClaudeCodeConfig/af: The cleanup Hook paired with `before`. It uses `before`'s reverse order and runs before the Agent's own after step: a LIFO mirror—`before` runs after Agent installation, while `after` runs before Agent cleanup. It runs only if execution reached the `before` point. A throw counts as an infrastructure error, and the after phase closes it with a teardown-failed diagnostic. See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/apiKey: Proxy / OpenAI API key. Falls back to the `CODEX_API_KEY` env var if omitted.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/baseUrl: OpenAI-compatible proxy base URL (e.g. `https://s2a.example.com/v1`). Falls back to the `CODEX_BASE_URL` env var if omitted.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/headers: Static HTTP headers to include with each request to a custom model provider, such as Cloudflare Access Service Token headers. Values are automatically redacted.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/env:
Extra environment variables injected into every Codex CLI process. The first `codex exec` and continuing `codex exec resume` use the same declaration; lifecycle Hooks started by Codex, dynamic MCP headers, and command subprocesses all inherit it. Values enter only through Sandbox command options: they are not concatenated into shell text or written to the before manifest, and are all redacted as potential sensitive values from timing, execution, and error evidence. `CODEX_API_KEY` still comes from `apiKey` or the same host environment variable; the Adapter's authentication value overrides a same-named key here.

An environment value does not enter carry identity. A non-sensitive value that changes behavior must also be declared in Experiment Flags or the owning Plugin identity; rotating credentials alone does not invalidate old results. `PATH` is Sandbox-managed and cannot be declared here. Its presence errors at factory construction; use the Sandbox factory's `pathPrepend` instead. See `docs/feature/sandbox/library/README.md`.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/mcpServ: Extra MCP servers, appended to `~/.codex/config.toml` during each Sandbox before. The stdio form (`command` / `args` / `env`) writes a `command` line in `[mcp_servers.<name>]`. The Streamable HTTP form (`url` / `headers`) writes the `url` line and headers in the `[mcp_servers.<name>.http_headers]` subtable.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/skills: Skills installed in the Sandbox: a local directory or file, or a Repo with a pinnable ref and optional enabled subset. They go to `.agents/skills/<name>/`, and a discovery instruction is written into AGENTS.md. Codex has no native Skill tool like Claude Code, so installing the file alone does not make it read it. See `memory/codex-no-native-skill-tool.md`.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/plugins: Native Codex Plugins: first connect a Marketplace, then install the named Plugin from it.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/configF: The path to a complete official-TOML Codex `config.toml` in the local project. It resolves relative to the project root that runs niceeval—the directory containing `niceeval.config.ts`—not inside the Sandbox. It accepts only a relative path within the project root. A path containing `..`, an absolute path, a `~` path, or a symlink that resolves outside the project root errors during before. Its original bytes are uploaded verbatim into the otherwise-empty user-level `~/.codex/config.toml` in the Sandbox. It does not inherit host configuration or parse and rewrite it. Reserved keys `model`, `model_provider`, `model_providers`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `mcp_servers`, and `otel` cause a before error when present. The manifest records only the project-relative path and byte SHA-256, not the contents.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/before: User Hooks run in array order after installation. They reuse SandboxCommand's narrow context and run only after the main configuration is written, MCP attached, Skills and Plugins installed, and the manifest written. They suit process actions that can run only after installed artifacts are ready, such as a Plugin's before script. A throw counts as an infrastructure error (`attempt errored`). See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
builtin-agent-config/CodexConfig/after: The cleanup Hook paired with `before`. It uses `before`'s reverse order and runs before the Agent's own after step: a LIFO mirror—`before` runs after Agent installation, while `after` runs before Agent cleanup. It runs only if execution reached the `before` point. A throw counts as an infrastructure error, and the after phase closes it with a teardown-failed diagnostic. See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/apiKey: API key for the OpenAI-compatible proxy. Falls back to the `BUB_API_KEY` env var if omitted.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/baseUrl: Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible proxy. Falls back to the `BUB_API_BASE` env var if omitted.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/skills: Skills installed in the Sandbox: a local directory or file, or a Repo with a pinnable ref and optional enabled subset. They go to `.agents/skills/<name>/`, and a discovery instruction is written into AGENTS.md. Bub has no native Skill-loading mechanism.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/version: Uses the fixed Bub 0.5.1 protocol. Omit this option or set it to `"0.5.1"`; any other version throws a `TypeError` when the Agent is defined.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/otelPlugi:
The git dependency for the OTel tape-store Plugin, the source of the timeline. When omitted, use NiceEval's default pin.

Custom Plugins must support the tape protocol of the fixed Bub 0.5.1 version.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/pythonPlu: Extra Python packages installed into the bub tool environment. Each Sandbox before adds them through `uv tool install … --with <pkg>`. The normalized package list enters the installation checkpoint key, so two Agent variants with different Plugin sets never reuse the same checkpoint; otherwise the second could silently receive the first variant's environment.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/before: User Hooks run in array order after installation. They reuse SandboxCommand's narrow context and run only after bub, Skills and Python packages are installed, and the manifest is written. A throw counts as an infrastructure error (`attempt errored`). See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
builtin-agent-config/BubConfig/after: The cleanup Hook paired with `before`. It uses `before`'s reverse order and runs before the Agent's own after step: a LIFO mirror—`before` runs after Agent installation, while `after` runs before Agent cleanup. It runs only if execution reached the `before` point. A throw counts as an infrastructure error, and the after phase closes it with a teardown-failed diagnostic. See Post-install scripts in `docs/feature/adapters/library/coding-agent-extensions.md`.
ui-message-stream-options/name: The Agent name used for Report and result-aggregation identity. Defaults to `"ui-message-stream"`.
ui-message-stream-options/url: The chat endpoint of the application under test. Use its full URL wherever the application is deployed. The function form resolves once per turn.
ui-message-stream-options/headers: Additional request headers, such as authentication. `ctx.telemetry.headers` for `traceparent` always merges in automatically.
ui-message-stream-options/body: Fields to merge into the request body in addition to `messages`, such as `(ctx) => ({ model: ctx.model })`. Fields whose value is `undefined` are automatically omitted during serialization.
ui-message-stream-options/projectToolCom: Lets the endpoint owner classify every logical tool call as command or not-command. An unknown call returns `undefined` and leaves actions coverage partial. NiceEval does not guess from a name or input.
ui-message-stream-options/denyReason: The reason sent with `approval-responded` when approval is denied. The application and SDK make it tool-result text that the model sees. A clear "do not retry" message measurably lowers the chance that a model repeats the same call.
ui-message-stream-options/settleMs: Milliseconds to wait after the stream ends before returning, giving application observability exporters such as BatchSpanProcessor time to export.
ui-message-stream-options/tracing: How an application with OTel delivers spans to the endpoint, for the waterfall. The event stream does not depend on it.
ui-message-stream-options/spanMapper: How an application with OTel normalizes spans, for the waterfall. The event stream does not depend on it.
config-fields/name:
The project name, shown in the hero (`<h1>`) at the top of `niceeval view`; it falls back to a generic title when omitted.
It can be a string, or text in multiple locales (such as `{ en: "...", "zh-CN": "..." }`) that switches with the view language.
config-fields/judgeProvider: The project-level default Judge Provider; an Eval or Experiment can replace the model or the whole Provider.
config-fields/reporters: The project-level Reporter list, for example for persisting or uploading results.
config-fields/maxConcurrency: The project-level default concurrency limit; the CLI flag or Experiment setting with the same name has higher priority (there is no environment-variable layer).
config-fields/maxBuildConcurrency: Run-level concurrency for preparing Sandbox images; independent of Attempt concurrency, with a safe default of 2 when omitted.
config-fields/maxBeforeCacheConcurrency: Run-level concurrency for preparing the PreparedArtifact prefix DAG; independent of build and Attempt concurrency.
config-fields/sandboxCache: The project-level before cache default; an Experiment or an explicit CLI flag can override it.
config-fields/timeoutMs: The project-level default timeout for one Attempt (milliseconds); the CLI flag, Experiment, or `EvalDef` setting with the same name has higher priority.
config-fields/telemetry:
OTLP receiver configuration, the only entry point inside a niceeval project (it does not read `NICEEVAL_OTLP_*` environment variables).
`port` pins the receiving port (fixed-port mode: a long-running service points `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` once at
`http://localhost:<port>/v1/traces`, and never changes it no matter how many Eval runs follow). When omitted, each run dynamically assigns
a temporary port (handed to the Adapter through `ctx.telemetry`). The tradeoff: with a fixed port, only one niceeval process can run on the machine at a time,
and an error occurs if another process holds that port; pick a free port and write it back here.
`host` is the receiver hostname reported to the Adapter (not the listening address, which is always `0.0.0.0`); it defaults to
`"127.0.0.1"`. Override it here only when you already provide a controlled tunnel or reachable route; a Docker Sandbox
puts the receiver inside the Sandbox by default and does not rely on an implicit host gateway.
config-fields/pricing:
User overrides or additions on top of the built-in price table (`o11y/prices.json`), looked up by model (see Observability
· Usage and Cost). A key can be an exact model name or a `provider/*` wildcard (to override self-hosted or gateway discounts in bulk per Provider);
exact keys take priority over wildcards. The Runner uses it to compute the budget estimate for `maxCost`; the Adapter physical-call
collector seals a matching explicit fixed profile as a call-bound estimate proof only when reported cost is absent.
Inspection reads only sealed proofs; it does not take mutable config as an operation input, and does not backfill historical calls by endpoint.
config-fields/pauseOnFailure: Suspend the Attempt and retain the Sandbox when an error or failure occurs, displaying native direct connect commands for debugging before cleanup.

usage-fields/inputTokens: Input tokens that missed the cache and are billed at full price; mutually exclusive with the two cache buckets.
usage-fields/cacheReadTokens: Input tokens served from a prompt-cache hit; a separate billing bucket, not included in inputTokens (omitted means the agent does not report it).
usage-fields/cacheCreationTokens: Input tokens written to the prompt cache; a separate billing bucket, not included in inputTokens (omitted means the agent does not report it).
usage-fields/reasoningTokens: The number of reasoning (thinking) tokens, a detail already included in outputTokens and listed separately for display; present only when the protocol actually provides it.
usage-fields/requests: The number of model requests that actually occurred. Omit it when the protocol does not provide a request count; never write 1 to fill it.
usage-fields/costUSD:
The actual USD cost measured by the gateway/adapter (it can only be brought back explicitly through `Turn.usage.costUSD`, and is never derived from
token usage or OTel spans). It and the top-level `estimatedCostUSD` (a price-table estimate) are two
independent facts under a one-way field contract: this field stores only the observed value; `estimatedCostUSD` always equals
the estimate from `estimateCost(model, usage, pricing)`, computed independently even when an observed value exists.
Neither overrides or backs up the other; an observed value never replaces or triggers the estimate.
expect-matchers/similarity: Normalized Levenshtein similarity; it is a continuous score and carries no default threshold or Verdict policy.
expect-matchers/includesUrl: A plain-text matcher that requires at least min distinct http(s) URLs.
expect-matchers/hasSections: A plain-text matcher that requires at least min Markdown headings.
expect-matchers/isTrue: A refinement matcher for value === true.
expect-matchers/isFalse: A refinement matcher for value === false.
expect-matchers/commandSucceeded: An exitCode === 0 matcher for CommandResult-like candidates; it does not read stdout / stderr.
expect-matchers/mapValue: Project a single value without replacing the original subject's refinement.
expect-matchers/mapEach: Project each complete item, retaining its material identity and order.
expect-matchers/filterWhere: Select only definite matches; an unknown selector makes the aggregate unavailable.
expect-matchers/countWhere: Compare an exact match count only after every item in a complete collection is known.
agent-def/AdapterCleanupContext/timeoutM: A fixed millisecond budget for the whole cleanup window; it is not renewed per callback.
agent-def/AdapterCleanupContext/deadline: The Unix millisecond deadline fixed when the cleanup window actually starts.
agent-def/AdapterCleanupContext/signal: Independent of the execution signal; aborts when the whole Adapter cleanup window reaches its deadline.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/models: Frozen application model selections for this Attempt.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/sealUsage: Close application usage admission and declare whether the recorded collection is complete.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/evalId: The public ID of the current Eval.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/experimen: The public ID of the current Experiment.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/attempt: The zero-based index of the current Attempt.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/signal: The Attempt execution signal; its reason distinguishes timeout from cancelled, and it is not used for the cleanup window.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/model: The model selected by the Experiment.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/reasoning: The reasoning effort selected by the Experiment.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/flags: The read-only flags the Experiment passes to the Adapter.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/progress: Updates the human-readable progress of the current Attempt.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/diagnosti: Appends a structured diagnostic to the current Attempt.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/log: Appends a log line to the current Attempt.
agent-def/AdapterCreateContext/onCleanup:
Registers release of an Attempt-local resource. Callbacks run in global LIFO order; one failure does not skip the rest.
Zero-argument callbacks can still be passed directly. The context passed in is frozen, and callbacks in the same cleanup window share one signal.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/name: The agent's display name/identifier, copied verbatim into `Agent.name`. It is not a registry lookup key; it is used only for display, result attribution, and the dedupe fingerprint.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/evidenceCoverag: This Adapter's normal evidence coverage declaration; use `completeEvidenceCoverage` for complete collection.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/before: Once per attempt. A Direct Agent does not receive a Sandbox; commonly used for one-time preparation such as opening connections and authentication.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/tracing: OTLP export configuration: how the system under test sends traces to the endpoint (env-based injection).
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/spanMapper: A thin mapper from native spans → canonical; omitted uses the generic heuristic. Affects only the waterfall.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/send: Once per turn: sends one turn's prompt directly to a function, SDK, or service endpoint, and parses the response into events. The author callback keeps the Promise ABI.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/classifySendFai: Optional send execution failure classifier: see `Agent.classifySendFailure`.
agent-def/DirectAgentDef/after:
Cleanup before the run ends, executed if and only if this attempt reached the `before` point (a `before` throw does not exempt it),
run once in finally.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/name: The agent's display name/identifier, copied verbatim into `Agent.name`. It is not a registry lookup key; it is used only for display, result attribution, and the dedupe fingerprint.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/evidenceCovera: This Adapter's normal evidence coverage declaration; use `completeEvidenceCoverage` for complete collection.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/sandbox: The Adapter's own Sandbox actions; an Agent cannot choose or contribute a template.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/ensure: A single entry or an array is normalized into Agent layers in declaration order.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/installers:
Paired installation layers; omitted means this adapter provides only the probe protocol, and on a miss the Runner
names the exact missing identity at `agent.ensure`. The factory normalizes an omission into an empty array.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/before:
Once per Attempt (not once per send): writes config.toml / authentication configuration (model/base/auth and other
runtime configuration that does not change within this Attempt). Probing, installing, and rechecking the CLI belong to `agent.ensure`. The runner calls it once after the Sandbox
is ready (after layer prepare/ensure/baseline) and before the first send; it returns no value.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/tracing: OTLP export configuration: how to make the CLI in the Sandbox send traces to the endpoint (env / config file), split out of before.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/spanMapper: A thin mapper from native spans → canonical; omitted uses the generic heuristic. Affects only the waterfall.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/send: Once per turn: runs the prompt (fresh / resume) and parses it into events. The author callback keeps the Promise ABI.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/classifySendFa: Optional send execution failure classifier: see `Agent.classifySendFailure`.
agent-def/SandboxAgentDef/after:
Cleanup before the Sandbox is destroyed, executed if and only if this attempt reached the `before` point (a `before` throw does not exempt it),
run once in finally.
agent-def/AgentContext/signal:
Soft cancellation signal: combines the attempt timeout, run-level interruption (user Ctrl+C), and the Eval's own interruption request
(see src/runner/attempt.ts). An adapter can optionally check it (or pass it straight to `fetch`) to exit
gracefully early, but it is not the only hard boundary: even if the adapter ignores it entirely, the runner uses
`Effect.timeoutTo` as a backstop to force after (stopping the Sandbox container).
agent-def/AgentContext/model: The model name used by this attempt, passed through from the Experiment's `model` field. Sandbox agents usually write it into configuration in before; direct agents usually use it in send to select the model.
agent-def/AgentContext/reasoningEffort: The model's reasoning effort; owned the same way as model: the Experiment decides it, and when omitted the agent's native default is not overridden.
agent-def/AgentContext/flags:
The Experiment's `flags` field passed through verbatim; its content and structure are entirely defined by the Experiment author
(such as `{ webResearch: true }`, `{ systemPrompt: "..." }`). The adapter reads its fields by its own convention;
the framework itself neither interprets nor validates the content. The name deliberately avoids the CLI-parsed
`flag` (run-level --timeout/--budget and so on); the two are unrelated concepts.
agent-def/AgentContext/experimentId:
The Experiment id derived from the path (the same source as result attribution `runWho` / `AgentRun.experimentId`); undefined when not running
through an Experiment (such as outside the CLI, constructing `AgentRun` directly). Typical uses:
a SandboxLayer command isolating cross-attempt infrastructure content per Experiment, or an adapter switching authentication / routing per Experiment.
It is a different dimension from `flags` (the concrete
values of Experiment conditions): this is only a stable identifier of "which Experiment is running" and carries no condition content.
agent-def/AgentContext/evalGroup: The eval group of the current Attempt; omitted for ungrouped Evals.
agent-def/AgentContext/attempt: The current Attempt reference filled in by the Runner; third parties constructing the context directly can omit it.
agent-def/AgentContext/telemetry:
Present only when OTel integration is configured (the agent's `tracing` block / the config's telemetry exists):
this run's OTLP traces receiver information (endpoint + env for env-based export).
How to hand it to the CLI is declared by the agent's `tracing` block: env-based spreads ctx.telemetry.env
into send; file-based writes configuration in tracing.configure. A remote HTTP integration's send
only needs to spread headers into the request headers (a new traceparent per turn); the endpoint is fixed by startup configuration
(defineConfig({ telemetry: { port } })) and is not passed from here.
agent-def/AgentContext/progress:
Scoped feedback: reports what is happening right now (turn / tool / install progress). Short-lived state: the Human profile
updates the active line, `agent`/`ci` do not print each one, and it does not enter the final result; do not call it for every token/delta.
The runner attributes it by the lifecycle phase the callback is currently in (agent.before / agent.run / agent.after);
the caller cannot impersonate another phase (see docs/feature/experiments/library/README.md).
agent-def/AgentContext/diagnostic:
Scoped feedback: reports problems that should remain after the run ends (protocol downgrade, incomplete data, cleanup issues).
A permanent event that lands in the attempt's diagnostics and each profile's permanent output; deduplicated by `dedupeKey`.
Even with level "error" it does not change Turn.status / verdict; throw when you cannot continue.
agent-def/AgentContext/log:
An explicit timeout breadcrumb. It also updates the Human active line, and the most recent entries are merged into the result's error information
on a timeout failure; do not use it to carry user messages, tool input, or other text meant only for short-lived display.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/workdi: The absolute path of the project/workspace root inside the Sandbox (the default cwd for agent commands, and where the git baseline is committed). Relative paths in every method resolve against it, and omitting `cwd`/`targetDir` also lands here.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/runCom:
Runs a single command; `args` are passed as separate argv entries and are not interpreted by a shell (no `&&`, pipes, or glob expansion).
Prefer it when you only want to run one executable, arguments come from external input, or you are worried about injection.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/runShe:
Runs a whole script interpreted by a shell (bash), supporting `&&`, pipes, `$()`, redirection, and so on.
Use it when you need to chain several commands or branch on conditions.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/runCom:
Runs a single command like `runCommand`, but throws `SandboxCommandExitError` on a non-zero exit. The error message includes
a bounded, cleaned, and redacted stderr tail; it falls back to stdout when stderr is empty. The full output is kept in the exception's
`result` field. A successful result's `exitCode` is fixed to `0` in its type.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/runShe:
Runs a shell script like `runShell`, but throws `SandboxCommandExitError` on a non-zero exit. The error summary,
full output, and successful result semantics are the same as `runCommandOrThrow`.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/readTe: Reads the text content (UTF-8) of a file inside the Sandbox. Throws when the file does not exist.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/writeT: Writes a UTF-8 text file inside the Sandbox; missing parent directories are created automatically.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/readBy: Reads a file's exact bytes inside the Sandbox; the public contract is not bound to Node Buffer.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/writeB: Writes a file's exact bytes inside the Sandbox; missing parent directories are created automatically.
sandbox-methods/SandboxOperations/pathEx: Checks whether a file or directory path exists inside the Sandbox.
sandbox-methods/SandboxTransferOperation: Transfers registered immutable content without exposing its host path.
sandbox-methods/Sandbox/nativeInstanceId: Provider-native instance selector for read-only diagnostics; absent when unavailable.
sandbox-methods/Sandbox/stop: Destroys the compute resources the Sandbox occupies (container/microVM). The Sandbox cannot be used after the call; whether repeated calls are safe varies by provider, so do not rely on it.
sandbox-methods/Sandbox/sandboxId: This Sandbox's stable identifier (each provider's native ID, such as a Docker container ID prefix); used to correlate session state of the same Sandbox across calls, and for log display.
sandbox-methods/Sandbox/otlpHost:
The placement capability of the OTLP receiver.
- `string`: the host receiver is reachable from inside the Sandbox through this hostname.
- `null`: the provider does not promise a connection back to the host; the runner tries to start an attempt-scope receiver inside the Sandbox.
  This does not guarantee tracing succeeds; when the image lacks the runtime the receiver needs, only a supplemental diagnostic is recorded.
`defineConfig({ telemetry: { host } })` can override it explicitly when the author already provides a controlled tunnel.
sandbox-methods/Sandbox/appendLog:
Optional: writes a line into the container's "main log" (which PID1 tails), so `docker logs` /
the Logs tab of the Docker UI shows the agent's turn-by-turn activity live. Implemented by the docker provider; others can omit it.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/sensitive:
Sensitive plaintext this command is known to handle (such as API keys, tokens, HTTP header values). The Runner still hands the
original values to the provider for execution, but replaces these values exactly before any timing / commands / execution / error evidence is persisted;
this array itself is never persisted and does not enter the fingerprint. Empty strings are ignored.

This is explicit provenance, not a secret scanner: unregistered free text cannot be reliably identified; if the caller encodes or splits a value
first, also register the encoded form that will actually appear in the command/output.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/env:
Adds/overrides environment variables for this command (layered on the Sandbox default environment without clearing defaults). `PATH` is a Sandbox
managed variable; each provider keeps the `PATH` it computed and does not guarantee it can be overridden here; to extend PATH, use
the Sandbox factory's `pathPrepend` (see docs/feature/sandbox/library/README.md "PATH: managed variable and
pathPrepend").
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/cwd: This command's working directory; omitted lands on `Sandbox.workdir`. Relative paths resolve against the workdir, and absolute paths are used as is.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/stream:
Also sends this command's output into the Sandbox's "native log stream" (so `docker logs` / the Logs tab of the Docker UI
shows it live). Turn it on for agent commands (codex exec / bub run / claude) to see the agent's raw output in the container
log. Each provider implements it (docker: tee into the file PID1 tails;
unsupported providers ignore it); how the log surfaces is the provider's business, and the adapter only declares intent.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/onStdout:
Called once for each stdout chunk of the command. The callback is only for short-lived feedback while running; the full stdout still appears verbatim
in the returned `CommandResult`. When the provider does not support real streaming, it calls it at least once with the full
stdout after the command ends; it must not drop it silently.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/onStderr: The stderr counterpart of `onStdout`; the full stderr is still kept in `CommandResult`.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/user:
Overrides the execution identity of this command; omitted = the Sandbox default identity (the identity the environment declares itself: the Docker image `USER`,
the Compose service `user:`, the E2B template default user; see
docs/feature/sandbox/library/README.md "Execution identity").

The semantics are consistent across providers, and each provider maps them to its own native mechanism (docker: `exec --user`; E2B:
`{ user }`; Vercel: accepts only `"root"`, mapped to `{ sudo: true }`, other values error).
Providers that run as root throughout treat it as a no-op; providers that cannot switch identity at all may not support it (and throw), but **the semantics of omission and
explicit values stay consistent** and do not vary by provider.
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/timeoutMs:
This command's own limit (milliseconds). **Omitting it is the norm**: when omitted, the limit = the remaining attempt deadline
(see docs/feature/sandbox/architecture/README.md "Deadline ownership"); the provider layer has no independent default.
Passing a shorter value explicitly is an intentional declaration and takes effect as usual; on hitting it, the attribution is recorded as "explicit command timeout".
sandbox-methods/CommandOptions/signal:
Cancels this managed command tree. The provider must confirm the command tree has terminated before the Promise settles; when it cannot terminate
precisely, it should retire the whole Sandbox rather than only closing the transport and leaving processes in the background.
defineeval-options/description: A one-sentence description shown in `niceeval list` and the view; purely informational, it does not affect scheduling or scoring.
defineeval-options/tags: Tags for CLI `--tag` filtering and view categorization; a selection dimension independent of id-prefix filtering.
defineeval-options/sandbox:
The Sandbox declaration layer this Eval contributes. Omitting it is equivalent to an empty command-only layer and provides no implicit template.
In each actual Eval × Experiment pair, exactly one side must provide a template-bearing layer.
defineeval-options/plugins: Explicit, immutable Eval Plugin occurrences; there is no directory inheritance.
defineeval-options/judge: A model string replaces only the model of the project's Judge Provider; a Provider instance replaces it entirely. The Experiment setting takes priority.
defineeval-options/timeoutMs: Overrides the project-level / CLI per-attempt timeout (milliseconds), only for this Eval.
defineeval-options/metadata: Arbitrary extra metadata, saved as Attempt Provenance; it does not take part in scheduling or scoring and is for custom reporters to consume.
defineeval-options/diff:
Adjusts the attribution exclusion list for the agent diff (Sandbox only; see docs/feature/eval/README.md): both arrays are
gitignore-style globs (relative to the workdir). By default .git/node_modules/build output/package-manager caches are excluded;
`ignore` adds exclusions on top of the default list; `include` has the highest priority and explicitly adds matching paths back.
The composition rule is fixed as "default ∪ ignore, then punched through by include", and the list is frozen at the ledger anchor.
test-context/note: Stores a JSON value or Quantity for display without registering an Assertion or affecting Verdict, score, or coverage.
judge-image/judgeImage: Capture PNG or JPEG bytes for an existing Judge call without sending a request.
judge-image/JudgeImageInput/body: Original encoded image bytes; copied synchronously, at most 4 MiB.
judge-image/JudgeImageInput/mediaType: Must match the encoded image. Paths, URLs and SVG are not accepted.
experiment-fields/models: Selects a model for each named model role of a custom Adapter; cannot be combined with the single-model shorthand.
experiment-fields/description: A one-sentence description shown in the view and CLI; purely informational, it does not affect scheduling or scoring.
experiment-fields/adapter: The Adapter implementation this Experiment uses.
experiment-fields/model: A single model (decided by the Experiment when the agent leaves it empty); omitted = use the agent's native default. To compare models, write several Experiment files instead of an array.
experiment-fields/reasoningEffort: The model's reasoning effort (such as "low"/"medium"/"high"; valid values depend on the specific model/adapter); omitted = use the agent's native default. Passed to the adapter and eval through ctx.reasoningEffort.
experiment-fields/flags:
Experiment conditions (the feature flags in an A/B), declared by the Experiment file; must be a flat scalar object
 (strings, finite numbers, or booleans only, validated when defineExperiment parses it). Passed to the adapter through ctx.flags,
 exposed to the eval as t.flags, and copied verbatim into the result snapshot's ExperimentRunInfo.flags.
experiment-fields/labels:
Report grouping labels: the Experiment's coordinates on each comparison axis (such as `{ line: "codex", memory: "mempal" }`).
Values are string | number (validated at parse time). The line between labels and `flags` is "does it change what happens in the attempt":
labels are not passed to ctx / t (the agent and eval cannot see them) and do not take part in the comparability configuration (changing them does not invalidate existing results);
they are only projected verbatim into the snapshot's `ExperimentRunInfo.labels` for report dimensions (`label()` / `numericLabel()`)
to group by. The default report recognizes the `line` key: when any Experiment in the group declares it, scatter points are grouped by line and connected.
See docs/feature/experiments/library/README.md "labels".
experiment-fields/attempts: How many times to repeat the same eval (each result counts as one attempt); defaults to 1 when omitted or when CLI `--attempts` overrides it.
experiment-fields/earlyExit:
Within a repetition (attempts > 1), whether to skip the remaining repeats after one attempt passes; defaults to false when omitted (`attempts` run in full to measure the complete pass rate).
 Turn it on explicitly to save cost when you only want to know whether it can pass.
experiment-fields/evals:
Which evals this Experiment covers: `"*"` for all, a string array matched by id prefix, or a custom predicate (which receives each discovered and fanned-out
read-only `EvalDescriptor`, with no path / execution fields exposed); omitted is equivalent to `"*"`. The predicate is evaluated once per
candidate eval of this invocation, and the result becomes the in-memory `selectedEvalIds` plan, not a filter called repeatedly at runtime
(see docs/feature/eval/library/README.md "EvalDescriptor" and docs/feature/experiments/library/README.md
"evals: iterate discovery results, choose your own").
experiment-fields/timeoutMs: Overrides the project-level / CLI per-attempt timeout (milliseconds), only for this Experiment.
experiment-fields/sandbox:
The Sandbox declaration layer this Experiment contributes. It is linked pairwise with the same field of each selected Eval;
in each pair, exactly one side provides a template-bearing layer.
experiment-fields/sandboxCache: The Host's execution cache policy; unlike the Sandbox declaration layer, this field does not take part in identity computation.
experiment-fields/plugins: The list of Plugin instances this Experiment declares explicitly, normalized by `defineExperiment()`.
experiment-fields/sandboxReuse: Reuse Sandboxes within the same Run; such runs are isolated from history carry in both directions.
experiment-fields/sharedState:
Declares shared external state this Experiment needs exclusively. Invocations with the same key in the same project
Coordination domain are mutually exclusive from before Experiment/Sandbox before until Sandbox after,
provider finalizers, and Experiment after have all finished; waiters do not create a Sandbox first,
and continue their own plan after acquiring the lease. It is not a state store, a transaction, or a cross-machine lock.
experiment-fields/budget:
This Experiment's estimated spend limit (USD). The scheduler accumulates the `estimatedCostUSD` of finished attempts; that value is
computed from the model, token usage, and the runtime/config pricing table, independent of the
observed `usage.costUSD` reported by the Provider / Adapter, which does not drive the budget. Once the estimate reaches the limit, the Experiment's remaining
attempts that have not started are skipped and `run:budgetExceeded` is reported once (attempts already in flight still finish).
experiment-fields/maxConcurrency:
This Experiment's own concurrency limit within this Invocation: the scheduler throttles only this Experiment's attempts; other Experiments in the batch are unaffected
and still run under the global concurrency (CLI / env / config / Sandbox default). Use it to serialize Experiments with shared state
(such as memory accumulated across evals: `maxConcurrency: 1` guarantees attempts run one by one in eval order),
or to slow down an Experiment that hits provider limits. A concurrency permit shares the attempt's lifetime: it is held from before Sandbox creation until
after and Sandbox destruction finish, and any wait along the way (including turn retry backoff) keeps holding it.
`maxConcurrency: 1` is therefore a strict critical section that the next attempt of the same Experiment cannot enter early.
It does not span Invocations; for shared external state across Invocations, declare `sharedState`.
experiment-fields/before:
The before side of the Experiment-level lifecycle hook pair: at most once per run, on the host side, for host resources that are "one per Experiment, shared by all attempts"
(tunnels, mock servers, license leases). Triggered by the first attempt of this Experiment that passes dispatch admission
(memoized: concurrent attempts wait for the same result; not run when all results are carried in).
before returns no value; write products to module-level variables, and `after` and agent / sandbox hooks in the same file read them from the closure;
the runner does not mediate values. If before throws, every Attempt of this Experiment gets an `errored` Verdict
(code `"experiment-setup-failed"`, phase `"experiment.before"`); other Experiments in the batch are unaffected.
The function body does not enter the fingerprint; after changing hook logic, use `--rerun all` to explicitly rerun everything.
See docs/feature/experiments/architecture/README.md "Experiment-level lifecycle".
experiment-fields/after:
The after side of the Experiment-level lifecycle hook pair: runs after all of this Experiment's attempts finish (also when the run is interrupted),
if and only if execution reached the before point. A before throw does not exempt it (a half-initialized scene also needs cleanup; after should guard closure variables
that may be unassigned); having no before declared does not prevent it from firing; it is skipped when no attempt is dispatched.
A throw or exceeding the 30s cleanup limit records only a run-level diagnostic (`experiment-teardown-failed`) and does not change the Verdict.
cli-flags/show/--json: Print the public Attempt query result as JSON.
cli-flags/show/--exp: Show one Experiment; repeat to show more.
